current.text: Allen is projected to start at center next to Evan Mobley, with James Harden, Donovan Mitchell and Peyton Watson.
Cleveland may play Mobley more at center in smaller lineups and close games with him there after adding Peyton Watson. Allen's minutes sometimes drop and he sits out some fourth quarters.
His minutes are at risk, and the expert does not see him reaching 30 minutes per game.
Big-man depth is very thin. Behind Mobley and Allen there is only Thomas Bryant, then Ernest Udeh Jr. and Khalifa Diop. Dean Wade is gone, which also removes the small-ball center option.
The weak backup center group and Wade's departure help Allen's role.

Cleveland gets a full season of James Harden. With Harden, Allen averaged 25 points and 13 rebounds per 36 minutes on 71% shooting with 23 usage. Without Harden, he averaged 19 points and 11 rebounds per 36 on 62% shooting.
A full season with Harden could lift his efficiency. If he shoots 66 to 67% on 21 to 22 usage, he could score about 17 points and be a top 70 player.
He had a knee injury late last season. There are no current injury concerns.
He finished around 69th to 79th last season depending on format, and 79th per game.

Experts value him in the 70 to 85 range with little upside. He is a solid pick around 85, and worth taking around 70 only if you need a center. One expert prefers Paul George at the same spot unless you need a center.
His ESPN rank of about 49 to 53 is too high. Experts call him a strong no and a top fade at that price.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With a March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3, then 2 games in the fantasy playoff weeks. The two-game week is finals week.
Cleveland's two-game week does not matter much for Allen.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games. Coach Kenny Atkinson is under pressure.

durable.text: Allen is a rebounding and FG% center who makes no threes. He no longer blocks many shots.
He usually shoots around 64% from the field. His true FG% level is probably between his recent low near 64% and his high near 71%.
He is a prime example of nine-cat fluff. Z-scores that include turnovers make him look better than he is.

note: Allen is a FG% and rebounds center who fits punt 3PM builds. Experts rank him around 70 to 85 and warn against his ESPN rank near 51, so pay close to Yahoo's 14 USD value or our league's 13 USD from last season, not ESPN-driven prices. Early in the season, check whether he gets close to 30 minutes or loses closing minutes to Mobley at center, and whether his FG% stays near 66% with Harden on the floor.
